_comment: Per-platform signature tables the scanner (check_rules.py) runs and verify_rules.py resolves rule tags against. Fields: id (stable; approved deviations and exceptions cite it), rule (the rule id it holds), group (optional: several signatures held by one rule tag, e.g. native-pattern), severity block|ratchet|advisory, scope added|tree, applies_to / excludes (path classes from paths.json; '*' = every class), files (optional glob list; default = the platform's extensions), pattern (regex over a line, and over the file's added lines joined without whitespace), paired (optional second regex that must also match), words (the failure's plain words). kind 'builtin' names a check implemented in code rather than a regex.

signatures.words: raw NSWindow/NSApplication reach-through from SwiftUI — window behavior belongs to SwiftUI's scene and window APIs
an NSViewRepresentable touching .window — a bridge view reaching into the hosting window's chrome
window-chrome override (standardWindowButton/styleMask/makeKeyAndOrderFront/titlebarAppearsTransparent) — replaces the platform's window controls
hiding the window toolbar (.toolbar(.hidden, for: .windowToolbar)) — removes the native title bar and traffic lights
a hand-rolled Route enum in place of NavigationStack — navigation belongs to the platform's navigation container
a full-screen scrim/dimming overlay used as a modal — modals belong to .sheet/.popover/.alert
an NSEvent key monitor — key handling belongs to the platform's focus and command system
focus APIs used to override key handling — the platform's command/shortcut system owns keys
a custom header/title bar in a hidden-title-bar window — the window's native title bar and toolbar own the header; if the platform provides the feature, use the feature
a hand-built tab bar — tab navigation belongs to TabView, even when every piece of the substitute is a native control
a hand-rolled search field (a TextField dressed with the search icon) — search belongs to .searchable
a hand-styled sidebar list — sidebars belong to NavigationSplitView, which provides the sidebar column and its styling itself
a hand-drawn progress indicator — progress belongs to ProgressView
a custom-built control where the platform provides one (Picker/Slider/Stepper/Toggle) — use the native control
module layering: feature modules never import each other, only the app target imports Data, Domain imports nothing app-side
user-facing text written as a literal in view code — it belongs in the string catalog under a semantic key
a colour or font size written as a literal — every visual value is a token in the theme file
a spacing, size or radius written as a number — use the theme's spacing tokens
a second theme or tokens file — styling has one home, the bound theme file; a brand swap is a one-file edit
a fact about the world outside the code written as a literal (a branch, a path, a host, a port, a fallback) — ask the system that owns it or read the one configured home
a secret written into the tree (a key, a token, a private key, a password) — secrets live in the platform's secure store, never in source
a secret- or data-shaped file added to the tree (an .env file, a key, a certificate, a database) — it never enters version control
